figures.caption: Figure 1: From trajectory IS to quotient-DAG weighting. (a) Trajectory IS assigns a likelihood ratio to each realized path. (b) The rollout tree shares prefixes but still represents distinct historyprefix nodes, even with repeated state labels. (c) A quotient DAG merges evaluation-equivalent prefixes into multi-parent nodes such as z4. The quotient likelihood ratio is the forward-flow ratio Fπ(z)/Fβ(z), not any single path ratio. each policy defines its forward flow, and the appropriate likelihood ratio is the target-to-behavior flow ratio Fπ(z)/Fβ(z). Per-decision IS, marginalized IS, and known-abstraction MIS are special cases of this construction, corresponding to different choices of equivalence relation.

Table 1: Finite-horizon MDP validation. Flows use logged trajectories only. Bold marks the lowest RMSE within each benchmark. †Neural GenDICE’s saddle-point optimization did not converge (defined as |V − V π| > 1) in 18/50 Sepsis and 14/50 ICU-Sepsis trials; reported statistics are on the 32 and 36 converged trials. Full 50-trial statistics are in Appendix G.

Figure 2: KuaiRec scaling. Left: joint slate-propensity wall-clock time for K!-enumeration, ForwardDP, and Gumbel-MC as slate size K increases; enumeration is extrapolated beyond K = 8, and Gumbel-MC uses 3 × 106 samples. Forward-DP avoids factorial enumeration while remaining exact. Right: downstream OPE RMSE for trajectory weights (OIS, DR) versus forward-flow weights (FF-OIS, FF-DR), using nusers = 300 and ntrials = 200. Within each K, the forward-flow variants reduce RMSE relative to their trajectory-weighted counterparts.

Table 4: Empirical violation of set-sufficiency under non-canonicalized prefix orderings on KuaiRec (M = 15, item-letter prompts). Two subset-sampling distributions are compared: random draws S ⊆ [M ] uniformly; β-induced draws S as the prefix at step |S| of a canonicalized β trajectory of length Kmax=8. Each row reports the median, 90th percentile, and mean (over user/subset draws) of the maximum pairwise TVD across orderings of S. Set-sufficiency requires all entries to be exactly 0; the larger entries on β-induced rows therefore quantify the bias the OPE estimator actually encounters under the deployed behavior policy. Each cell uses 160 (user, subset) draws.

Figure 3: Bias versus standard-deviation decomposition of RMSE on the finite-horizon MDP benchmarks (visualizing Table 1). Bars on log scale. STAR on Sepsis and FQE on ICU-Sepsis are biasdominated; OIS is variance-dominated on both benchmarks; the DICE-family estimators (DualDICE, GenDICE) are bias-dominated on both, with bias an order of magnitude larger than FF-WIS; FF-OIS and FF-WIS are small on both axes. GenDICE bars use trimmed-trial statistics (see Table 1).

Figure 4: K = 4 off-policy model-selection metrics by estimator (visualizing Table 3). Higher is better for top-1 and Spearman; lower is better for regret. Best per panel: Tree-DR (top-1, Spearman) and DP-OPCB-DR (regret), both Forward-DP-enabled.
